content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge labels the single verse UNDERDETERMINED because it admits two readings, which is exactly the kind of single-verse ground the rule governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings;", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.", "room": "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. I weighed whether the judge's phrase admits both readings means the verse carries two senses at once (so it is not open) or only that the single verse does not settle the link (a forbidden ground for UNDERDETERMINED).", "why": "The judge treats the verse's dual readings as a reason for UNDERDETERMINED, but K-S2 says a verse carrying two senses is not open and both senses stand."}
